questions.question: Shri Jatin Goswami received several honours for his contribution to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 3.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India awarded him the fourth highest civilian honour of the Padma Shri, in 2008, for his contributions to **Sattriya dance.**
 
• **Sattriya dance** is a classical dance form that originated in the Indian state of **Assam.**
 
• It is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India.
 
• Sattriya dance is closely associated with the Sattras, which are Vaishnavite monasteries in **Assam**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India and originated in the southern state of Tamil Nadu**.

 
 
• It is a highly expressive and intricate dance style that combines graceful movements, intricate footwork, hand gestures (mudras), facial expressions, and storytelling.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Kathak is a classical dance form of India that originated in the northern regions, particularly in the states of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.**

 
 
• 
 
It is known for its rhythmic footwork, intricate gestures, fast spins, and expressive storytelling.

 
 
• 
 
Kathak has both Hindu and Muslim influences, as it evolved as a blend of the Hindu temple traditions and the Persian and Mughal court dance traditions.

 
 
• 
 
The word **"Kathak"** is derived from the Sanskrit word "katha," which means story. Thus, Kathak is often referred to as the "dance of storytelling" because it emphasizes narrative elements through mime, facial expressions, and body movements.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Manipuri dance is one of the classical dance forms of India, originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.**

 
 
• 
 
It is known for its grace, fluidity, and devotion to the theme of Radha and Krishna, the divine lovers from Hindu mythology.

 
 
• 
 
Manipuri dance is deeply rooted in the religious and cultural traditions of Manipur and has a rich history that dates back centuries.

questions.question: The Nobel Prize for Physics 2022 has been given in the field of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Nobel Prize in Physics 2022 **was awarded jointly to** Alain Aspect, John F. Clauser and Anton Zeilinger "for experiments with entangled photons, establishing the violation of Bell inequalities and pioneering quantum information science"**
 
• **The Nobel Prize** is a set of prestigious international awards given annually in several categories, including** Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences.**
 
• The prizes were established by the will of **Alfred Nobel, a Swedish inventor, engineer, and industrialist, in 1895.**
 
• **Nobel's** will specified that the prizes should be awarded to individuals who have made significant contributions in their respective fields, thereby benefiting humanity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here are some key points about the Nobel Prize:
 
• **Categories:** The Nobel Prizes are awarded in the following categories:
 
 
• **Physics:** Recognizes outstanding contributions to the field of physics.
 
• **Chemistry: **Honors exceptional achievements in the field of chemistry.
 
• **Physiology or Medicine:** Acknowledges advancements in medical research and healthcare.
 
• **Literature:** Awards remarkable literary work.
 
• **Peace:** Recognizes efforts to promote peace and resolve conflicts.
 
• **Economic Sciences: **Added later in 1968 by the Swedish central bank and named the "Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel." It is awarded for notable contributions to the field of economics.
 
• **Selection Process: **The Nobel Prizes are awarded based on the decisions made by various committees and organizations. Each category has a specific organization responsible for the selection process. For example, the Nobel Prize in Physics is awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, while the Nobel Peace Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee.
 
• **Nomination and Laureates:** The nomination process involves a rigorous selection of candidates. Nominations are typically invited from qualified individuals and organizations, such as university professors, previous laureates, and members of international organizations. The nominations are then reviewed, evaluated, and shortlisted by experts in each respective field. Finally, the laureates are chosen by the responsible committees or organizations.
 
• **Recognition and Ceremony: **Nobel laureates receive a diploma, a gold medal, and a cash prize. The Nobel Prize ceremony takes place annually on December 10th in Stockholm, Sweden, except for the Nobel Peace Prize, which is awarded in Oslo, Norway. The laureates are invited to give lectures and participate in various events, contributing to the exchange of knowledge and ideas.
 
• **Significance and Impact:** The Nobel Prize is considered one of the highest honors in their respective fields. Winning a Nobel Prize brings global recognition and often leads to increased opportunities for further research, collaboration, and funding. The prizes have had a significant impact on advancing scientific, literary, and peace-related endeavors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the objectives of the NITI Aayog?

options.text: To develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level
To design and print new currency notes and to bring them in circulation
To pay special attention to the sections of our society that may be at risk of not benefiting adequately from economic progress.
To evolve a shared vision of national development priorities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The design and printing of currency notes and their circulation is not one of the objectives of the **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India).**
 
• **The NITI Aayog** is a policy think tank of the Government of India that primarily focuses on strategic and long-term planning for the country's development.
 
• It acts as a platform for cooperative federalism, fostering the involvement of **states in policy formulation and implementation**.
 
• The responsibility for the design, printing, and circulation of currency notes in India lies with the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, which is the central banking institution of the country.
 
• **The RBI **is responsible for formulating and implementing monetary policy, issuing currency notes, and regulating the overall banking and financial system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The NITI Aayog, or the National Institution for Transforming India,** is a policy think tank of the **Government of India.**
 
• It was established on** January 1, 2015**, to replace the erstwhile Planning Commission.
 
• **The NITI Aayog's primary objective **is to provide strategic and long-term policy inputs to the central and state governments to foster sustainable and inclusive development across various sectors of the Indian economy.
 
• **The key functions and objectives of the NITI Aayog include:**
 
 
• **Formulating strategic and long-term development plans: **The NITI Aayog formulates and recommends strategic plans, medium-term and long-term development frameworks, and policies for various sectors of the economy.
 
• **Cooperative federalism:** The NITI Aayog promotes cooperative federalism by fostering the involvement of state governments in policy formulation and implementation, ensuring their active participation and contribution in the planning process.
 
• **Policy research and innovation: **The NITI Aayog conducts research, analysis, and evidence-based policy studies on various social and economic issues to identify challenges, suggest innovative solutions, and provide policy recommendations to the government.
 
• **Monitoring and evaluation: **The NITI Aayog monitors and evaluates the implementation of policies and programs, assesses their outcomes, and suggests mid-course corrections, if required, to achieve desired development goals.
 
• **International cooperation: **The NITI Aayog facilitates international cooperation and exchange of best practices in policy planning and development with other countries and international organizations.
 
• **Collaborative platforms: **The NITI Aayog provides a platform for collaboration and dialogue among various stakeholders, including government agencies, experts, academicians, industry representatives, and civil society organizations, to foster participative and inclusive policy-making.
 
• It's important to note that the NITI Aayog's role is primarily advisory in nature, and the responsibility for implementing policies and executing projects lies with the respective ministries and departments of the central and state governments.

questions.question: When was the Treaty of Purandar signed between Shivaji and Jai Singh I?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1665**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Treaty of Purandar, 1665 was signed between the Jai Singh I and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
 
• This treaty was signed on 11th June 1665.
 
• Raja Jai Singh was signed on behalf of the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• Shivaji agreed to surrender 23 forts to the Emperor while the Emperor recognized Shivaji’s authority over 12 forts including Rajgarh and its revenue.
 
• Shivaji promised to supply for imperial service 5000 soldiers under his son Shambhaji and the Emperor agreed to assign a suitable jagir for their maintenance.
 
• Shivaji declined to accept any mansab but promised to fight on behalf of the emperor whenever demanded.
 
• There were some secret clauses in the treaty as well, which provided for Shivaji’s participation in the war against Bijapur on behalf of the Emperor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Jai Singh, I became the King of Amber and Head of the Kachwaha Rajput at the age of 10.
 
• Raja Jai Singh is the descendant of Raja Man Singh, and he is one of the famous nav-ratnas of Emperor Akbar. 
 
• The fort of Amer (or Amber) near Jaipur, Rajasthan is used to be their capital.
 
• Shivaji is the founder of the Maratha Kingdom in India.
 
• In 1674, he was formally crowned as the Chhatrapati (Monarch) of his realm at Raigad.
 
• Shivaji established a competent and progressive civil rule with the help of a disciplined military and well-structured administrative organisations.

questions.question: _____ is calculated by dividing the nominal GDP in a given year by the real GDP for the same year and multiplying it by 100.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP Deflator**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **GDP deflator **is an economic indicator that measures inflation or deflation in an economy.
 
• **It is calculated by dividing the nominal GDP by the real GDP and multiplying the result by 100.**
 
• **Nominal GDP** is the value of all goods and services produced in an economy, unadjusted for inflation.
 
• **Real GDP** is the value of goods and services produced in an economy, adjusted for inflation.
 
• **The GDP **deflator helps compare the economic output of different years by adjusting for changes in price levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disposable Income:**

 
 
• Disposable income refers to the** income remaining after deduction of taxes and other mandatory charges.**
 
• It is the amount of money available for spending and saving after all deductions.
 
• Disposable income does not directly relate to **GDP calculations or inflation adjustments.**
 
 
 
• **Real Income:**
 
 
• Real income refers to the** income of individuals or nations, adjusted for inflation.**
 
• It reflects the purchasing power of income, taking into account changes in price levels.
 
• Real income is **not a measure of inflation or deflation, but rather a measure of the true value of income in terms of goods and services.**
 
 
 
• **Per Capita Income:**
 
 
• **Per capita income is a measure of the average income earned per person in a certain area or region.**
 
• It is calculated by dividing the total income of a region by its population.
 
• Per capita income is** not directly related to inflation, deflation, or GDP calculations, but is a useful metric for comparing living standards and economic development between regions.**

• **The ICC Women's T20 World Cup is an international championship of Twenty20 International cricket for women.**
 
• It is **organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC), the governing body of international cricket.**
 
• The inaugural tournament took place in **England in 2009, coinciding with the men's T20 World Cup.**
 
• The tournament was** initially held every two years,** but from 2020 onwards, **it is held every year except for the years when the Women's Cricket World Cup (50-over format) is scheduled.**
 
• The format of the tournament** usually involves a round-robin group stage followed by knockout stages, leading to a final match to determine the world champion.**

• It provides an** international platform for female cricketers and has substantially increased the visibility and popularity of women's cricket.**

questions.question: Which of the following earthquake waves are surface waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**L waves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **L waves, or Love waves, are one type of surface wave in seismic activity.**

 
 
• Named after British mathematician** A.E.H. Love, **who first mathematically predicted their existence.
 
• **Love waves move the ground from side to side in a horizontal plane perpendicular to the direction of propagation.**
 
• As they travel along the **Earth's surface, they cause horizontal shearing and produce entirely horizontal motion.**
 
• L waves are the slowest of all** seismic waves and therefore the last to be recorded by seismographs.**
 
• These waves are particularly damaging to the foundations of structures due to their horizontal motion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **P waves:**

 
 
• P waves, or **Primary waves, **are **body waves that travel through the interior of the Earth.**
 
• They are the fastest seismic waves and thus the first to be detected by seismographs.
 
• P waves cause particles to move in the same direction as the waves, creating a push-and-pull motion.
 
 
 
• **S waves:**
 
 
• S waves, or** Secondary waves, are also body waves that move through the Earth's interior.**
 
• **They are slower than P waves but faster than surface waves.**
 
• S waves cause particles to move perpendicular to the wave direction, **creating an up-and-down or side-to-side motion.**
 
 
 
• **R waves:**
 
 
• Also known as the Rayleigh wave.
 
• It has both compressional and shear motions.
 
• These waves result from the interaction of P-waves and vertically polarized S-waves with the surface and can exist in any solid medium.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6c65456702f76c756160752cb845963bdccf7379fbb8c83f885fb21fe48f83b.png]

questions.question: Which among the following alloys is made up of copper and zinc?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dutch Metal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dutch Metal, **also known as **Dutch gold or composition gold, is an alloy primarily composed of copper and zinc.**
 
• It's an alloy of** approximately 85% copper and 15% zinc.**
 
• Despite its name, **Dutch Metal doesn't contain gold.**
 
• It's often used because of its **gold-like appearance in applications such as gilding and jewellery.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monel Metal:**

 
 
• **​**This is an alloy primarily **composed of nickel and copper.**
 
• It's highly resistant to corrosion and acids, **and it's used in various applications, such as marine and chemical environments.**
 
 
 
• **Magnalium:**
 
 
• **​**It's an aluminium alloy that's mixed with** 1.5% to 2% magnesium.**
 
• It's lighter than aluminium and is often used in applications where lightweight strength is needed, such as in the construction of aircraft.
 
 
 
• **Rolled Gold:**
 
 
• **Also known as gold-filled,** it's a** hybrid material composed of a thin layer of gold that's bonded to a base of either silver or a base metal. It's primarily used in jewellery.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of river Kaveri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Musi**__.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Musi river** is not a tributary of the river Kaveri.
 
• **It is a tributary of the Krishna River, which is another major river in Southern India.**
 
• The Musi River is primarily located in the** Telangana state of India.**
 
• It passes through **the city of Hyderabad and is known for its historical significance in the city's development.**
 
• The river is infamous for causing one of the worst floods in** Hyderabad's history, known as the Great Musi Flood of 1908.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhavani:**

 
 
• The** Bhavani River is a significant tributary of the Kaveri River, originating from the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It is the **second-longest river in Tamil Nadu and contributes significantly to the water volume of the Kaveri River.**
 
 
 
• **Hemavati:**
 
 
• The **Hemavati River is another important tributary of the Kaveri River.**
 
• It originates from the **Western Ghats in Karnataka and joins the Kaveri River at Krishnarajasagara.**
 
 
 
• **Kabini:**
 
 
• The **Kabini River, also known as Kapila, is a significant tributary of the Kaveri River.**
 
• It originates in **Kerala and flows eastward to join the Kaveri River in Karnataka.**
 
• The **Kabini River is known for the Kabini Forest Reserve, a popular wildlife destination.**

questions.question: In a ______ network, all nodes are connected to a single communication line and share it for all their communication needs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Multi-access bus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a multi-access bus network, **all nodes (computers, printers, etc.) are connected to a single communication line (the bus).**
 
• This network type is called **'multi-access' because all nodes share and have access to the same communication line.**
 
• Information sent from one node travels along the bus to all other nodes on the network.
 
• It is simple and less expensive to install and expand.
 
• **However, as the number of nodes increases, the efficiency of the network can decrease because of data collisions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ring Topology-

 
 
• In Ring Topology each node connects to two other nodes and forms a single continuous pathway for signals through each node.
 
• It connects the workstations in a closed loop.
 
• Data is transmitted around the ring in one direction only.
 
• A break in the ring causes the entire network to fail.
 
• There is no signal loss in the Ring Topology.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8f777f2003323826b44f12f7e450e033573e98e5598faaeff78bc6281d388ac.png] 

 

 

 

​

 
• Bus Topology-

 
 
• In Bus Topology nodes are connected to a common half-duplex link called a bus or backbone.
 
• Each workstation is connected to the next workstation in a point-to-point fashion.
 
• The common implementation of this topology is Ethernet.
 
• This topology is used only in comparatively small networks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/062dbeec6343e1c42ec256538d48abae542ff9a86374676fdeae015531f94efb.png] 

 
• Star Topology- 

 
 
• In this network, topology nodes are connected to a central hub.
 
• Nodes communicate across the network by passing data through the hub.
 
• Failure in one of the terminals does not affect any other terminal.
 
• This network topology is used to connect terminals to a large time-sharing host computer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b246a46959e79ea499476474419dc185f8ea907e0a37245bea26c532b6b9f76.png] 

 
• Mesh Topology- 

 
 
• In this network, topology devices are connected with many redundant interconnections between network nodes.
 
• Failure in one of the computers does not cause the network to break down.
 
• This topology is used in the critical connection of host computers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf6bb3f9bc6023e5a7801599c0af06f55a60824edfa1419e1a29b2f3f39841ed.png]

questions.question: If unemployment continues for long-term in a country, it is called ______ unemployment.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chronic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chronic Unemployment:**

 
 
• Chronic unemployment refers to** long-term unemployment typically caused by structural problems in the economy.**
 
• It is not due to the usual ups and downs of the business cycle but rather persists even in good economic times.
 
• Those who suffer from **chronic unemployment lack the skills or education needed for new jobs or live in parts of the country where jobs are scarce.**
 
• This type of unemployment can lead to a vicious cycle of** joblessness, poverty, and social issues.**
 
• It requires concerted policy efforts to resolve, such as** retraining programs, education reform, and economic development initiatives.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Casual Unemployment:**

 
 
• This refers to temporary **unemployment which occurs when workers are laid off or lose their jobs due to seasonal changes in demand or supply in certain industries.**
 
 
 
• **Technological Unemployment:**
 
 
• This type of unemployment is caused by **technological changes or automation that render certain jobs obsolete.**
 
• Workers displaced by technology **need to acquire new skills to find employment in other sectors.**
 
 
 
• **Frictional Unemployment:**
 
 
• This is a type of **short-term unemployment that occurs when people are between jobs or are looking for their first job.**
 
• **It's a natural part of the job market as people move between roles and careers.**

questions.question: Silicon dioxide is found mostly in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sand:**

 
 
• Sand is primarily made of tiny granules of quartz, **which is essentially silicon dioxide (SiO2).**
 
• Silicon dioxide is a chemical compound that is an oxide of silicon.
 
• **It is the most abundant mineral in the Earth's crust.**
 
• Apart from **sand, silicon dioxide is also found in quartzite, amethyst, agate, and other minerals**.
 
• Due to its** hardness and resistance to weathering, it forms the majority component of sand.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sugar:**

 
 
• **Sugar is a sweet crystalline substance **obtained from various plants, especially sugarcane and sugar beet.
 
• Its chemical formula is** C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁**, which is quite different from** silicon dioxide.**
 
 
 
• **Salt:**
 
 
• Salt, or sodium chloride** (NaCl), is a mineral composed primarily of sodium and chlorine.**
 
• It is different from silicon dioxide both in its chemical structure and physical properties.
 
 
 
• **Slaked Lime:**
 
 
• **Slaked lime, or calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2)**, is produced when **quicklime (calcium oxide, CaO)** is **mixed,** or** 'slaked',** with **water (H2O)**.

questions.question: IBM 360 was developed in which of the following generations of computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Third Generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The IBM System/360 **was announced and developed in the** mid-1965s, during the period associated with third-generation computers.**
 
• Third-generation computers were defined by the use of **integrated circuits (ICs) or semiconductor chips, which represented a significant advancement over the previous generation's technology.**
 
• The** System/360** was a groundbreaking series of** compatible mainframe computers, allowing customers to upgrade from lower-cost models to larger systems without having to rewrite their applications.**
 
• It also introduced the** 8-bit byte to the commercial world, which remains a fundamental data management unit today.**
 
• **The S/360** was not just a computer but a whole series of computers that helped to establish the concept of a computer **"family".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation:**

 
 
• These computers** (late 1946s to mid-1959s) were based on vacuum tubes.**
 
• They were large, expensive, and generated a lot of heat.
 
• Examples include the **ENIAC and UNIVAC.**
 
 
 
• **Second Generation:**
 
 
• Second generation computers** (mid-1959s to mid-1965s) moved from vacuum tubes to transistors, which were smaller, faster, cheaper, and more reliable.**
 
• **IBM's 7000 series belongs to this generation.**
 
 
 
• **Fourth Generation:**
 
 
• These computers** (1971 to the mid-1980s) are characterized by microprocessors which contain many, sometimes millions, of ICs.**
 
• **Personal computers, such as the IBM PC, fall into this category.**
